newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia 1997 sugar imports seen 1.1 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia 1997 sugar imports seen 1.1 mln tonnes.

text.p: Indonesia is expected to import between 1.0 million and 1.1 million tonnes of mixed sugar this year, almost unchanged from 1996, traders said on Monday.

"This year's imports are expected to be more or less the same as last year's amount of 1.0-1.1 million tonnes," one trader said. "If Indonesia is showing any interest in the market now, it is possibly for January or February shipments."
Indonesian white sugar imports are the monopoly of the state logistics agency BULOG. The government in July allowed sugar producers to import raw sugar.
The traders said that reports of Indonesian interest in buying white sugar emerging from London currently were probably part of BULOG's import schedule.
"BULOG frequently buys forward months, not prompt shipment," one trader said. "It is a regular buyer of sugar from Thailand and Brazil."
"I don't think that Indonesia's intended purchase of white sugar has anything to do with the rupiah situation," he said. "I don't see anything untoward."
The Indonesian currency had fallen sharply against the U.S. dollar in recent weeks, with the rupiah shedding some 27 percent of its value since the beginning of the year.
BULOG officials were not immediately available for comment.
Rante Tondok, director-general of plantations, had said Indonesia's 1996 sugar production was expected to have fallen short of the targeted 2.4 million tonnes.
He said sugar production rose to 2.1 million tonnes in 1995 from 1.6 million tonnes in 1983.
